goods_industries.name: Agriculture, Forestry, Fishing & Hunting
goods_industries.analysis: Canola leads Canada's field crop complex at 21.8 Mt for 2025-26, up 13% year-over-year and 19% above the five-year average.1 Total Canadian grain production reached a record 107 Mt in 2025, with carry-out stocks projected to rise 67%.1 China's tariff reduction on canola from approximately 85% to 15% reopens a $4B market for Canadian exporters.2 Wheat futures sit at $601.75/bu while corn trades at $465.25/bu.3 The federal government allocated $75M through the AgriMarketing Program (2026-31) for market diversification.4 Prices for most principal field crops are forecast lower year-over-year except soybeans and mustard seed.1 The pipeline tracks 13 projects valued at $4.7B, led by a Quebec biofuel facility ($1.2B), Saint John Pulp Mill upgrades in New Brunswick ($1.1B), and Hinton Pulp Mill expansion in Alberta ($584M).5

sources.title: Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada — Field Crop Report

goods_industries.name: Mining, Quarrying, and Oil & Gas Extraction
goods_industries.employment_trend: Drilling rig count up 6% YoY; 5,709 wells projected for 2026
goods_industries.analysis: WTI crude trades at $86.25/bbl amid Strait of Hormuz transit concerns, while Brent sits at $107.31/bbl.1 Gold reached $4,572/oz and copper holds at $5.53/lb.1 CAOEC projects 213 active drilling rigs in 2026, up from 201 in 2025, with 5,709 wells forecast (+3%).2 The federal government committed $3.6B in new critical minerals programs, with $165.2M allocated to 22 projects unlocking $434M in investment across eight provinces.3 The Critical Minerals Partnerships Alliance has mobilized $18.5B in Canadian projects.3 Fast-tracked developments include Foran Mining's McIlvenna Bay copper-zinc project in Saskatchewan and the Red Chris copper expansion in BC (+15% annual copper output).4 An Indigenous-led floating LNG terminal on BC's northern coast is nearing final investment decision in 2026.2 The Critical Minerals Sovereign Fund provides $2B over five years, supplemented by the First and Last Mile Fund at $1.5B over four years.3 The pipeline tracks 397 projects valued at $252.3B, anchored by LNG Canada ($40.0B) and KSM gold/copper ($8.4B).5

goods_industries.name: Utilities
goods_industries.employment_trend: Growing; clean energy transition driving new hires
goods_industries.analysis: Natural gas trades at $3.05/MMBtu, providing baseline generation cost inputs while the sector accelerates its transition to renewables.1 CanREA reports installed wind, solar, and storage capacity will grow by one-third in four years and double in a decade, with approximately 24 GW announced and ~8 GW expected online by 2029.2 Ontario's Long-Term 2 battery energy storage system awards are expected in Q2 2026, while Quebec and British Columbia are procuring thousands of MW of renewables.2 The Canada Energy Regulator projects power generation to increase 30%-100% by 2050, driven partly by AI data centre demand.3 OPG's Darlington SMR project ($20.9B, four BWRX-300 units totalling 1,200 MW) applied for its Licence to Operate in March 2026, with basemat placement scheduled for summer 2026.4 SaskPower's BWRX-300 deployment targets the mid-2030s, with a construction decision expected in 2029.4 Federal funding of $28.9M was allocated for 12 clean energy projects spanning CCUS, renewables, and smart grid technologies.5 The pipeline tracks 1,306 projects valued at $505.9B, led by LNG Canada Phase 1 ($47.9B) and the Deep Geological Repository ($26.0B).5
goods_industries.commodity_price: Natural Gas $3.05/MMBtu; Uranium linked to SMR pipeline

goods_industries.name: Construction
goods_industries.employment_trend: Civil construction +30% projected growth; overall sector mixed
goods_industries.analysis: Lumber trades at $339/MBF, aluminum at $3,423/lb, and copper at $5.53/lb, forming the primary material cost base for the sector.1 February 2026 building permits totalled $12.1B, down 8.4% month-over-month, with non-residential collapsing 24.0% to $4.0B.2 Institutional permits fell 51.5%, commercial declined 7.2%, and industrial dropped 9.6%.2 On the residential side, 21,000 multi-unit and 3,900 single-family dwellings were authorized, with the 12-month multi-family total reaching 255,500 units.2 Civil construction is the only major category projected for growth in 2026, at approximately 30% expansion.3 Federal budget commitments include $25B for housing, $30B for defence/security, $110B for productivity, and $115B for infrastructure.4 The Build Communities Strong Fund launched April 7, 2026 with $51B over 10 years; the first tranche covers 13 projects at $300M federal.4 The pipeline tracks 1,033 projects valued at $210.3B, led by the Ontario Line ($27.4B) and GO Expansion ($26.1B).5

goods_industries.name: Manufacturing
goods_industries.employment_trend: EV battery plants adding jobs; traditional auto declining
goods_industries.analysis: Aluminum at $3,423/lb, copper at $5.53/lb, and nickel (linked to EV battery supply chains) form the key input costs for Canadian manufacturing.1 Auto production is expected to decline approximately 4% in 2026, following 2025 output of 1.2M+ vehicles (-5.4% YoY).2 Auto exports fell 21.2% to $5.4B in January 2026 (the lowest since September 2021), then recovered 30.2% in February.2 The federal government allocated $3B through the Strategic Response Fund plus $100M via the Regional Tariff Response Initiative for the auto sector.3 EV sales targets stand at 75% by 2035 and 90% by 2040.3 VW PowerCo's St. Thomas gigafactory completed primary concrete foundations and will become Canada's largest manufacturing plant.4 NextStar Energy in Windsor commenced battery module production.4 An additional $11.7M was allocated for 15 EV charging projects installing 1,600+ chargers nationally.5 The pipeline tracks 49 projects valued at $67.3B, including the Dow Fort Saskatchewan Path2Zero expansion ($10.1B).5
